issue: cinatra#2802 — install-semantics S5: the settings access picker re-anchors the install row
host: a lane host (a real dev instance, real platform-admin session, real Postgres; no mockups)
fixture: The organization-anchored install row and a second organization holding an ARCHIVED row of the same package were seeded directly in the canonical writer shape (the same columns _internalInsertInstalledExtension writes), because every bundled package on a fresh instance is already installed at the platform tier and the marketplace therefore offers no organization install to run. Everything after the fixture is the shipped path: the real settings page, the real picker, the real server action.

dbAfterWiden.movedRowId: unchanged — the same install row id throughout
dbAfterWiden.supersededOrganizationRow: the second organization's ACTIVE row was archived in place by the same transaction

dbAfterNarrow.archivedRows: left archived — nothing revives by itself

dbAfterAnchorConflict: unchanged — the refused save wrote nothing
divergences: Screenshot (c): the archived list does NOT surface the superseded organization row while the workspace row is live. That is the S4 rule already in the code (an organization row of a package that has a live workspace row is filtered out of the card model; it becomes addressable again once the workspace install is gone), not an S5 regression. The screenshot therefore shows the Archived filter selected after the widening, and the supersession itself is proven at the database layer (dbAfterWiden) and by the real-Postgres fixtures.

Screenshot (b1): the active installed list does not draw a card for this package on this instance — its artifact descriptor comes from the platform-tier row, which the fixture archived so the settings page would resolve the organization row unambiguously. The marketplace card (b2) carries the reach statement the issue names, and it reads exactly 'Installed (Workspace: All)'.
